evidence_review:
A few years ago my husband was in a nursing home - now called Skilled Nursing, which I suppose sounds better than NURSING home.
It was there while visiting him each day that I had my first taste of BOOST.  They gave it to him every time he wanted a drink and
often brought an extra for me.  I have to admit I don't prefer supplemental, energy or dietary drinks but at the time, they sufficed.

Now I am trying this out for an entirely different reason.  I now live in a retirement community and because some high-calorie things are
served in our dining room daily, I have gained weight.  So, someone told me that these  drinks could cut down on your calories, I
decided to give it a try.

Still not my favorite but neither are the extra pounds.  If I could add a scoop of vanilla ice cream this review would probably sound better.
But as that would defeat my purpose, I have been trying this Rich Chocolate Boost out.  Certainly it does not rank up there with the best
drink I ever had but considering all those vitamins, etc. I didn't expect much.  These are 4 oz cans (Compact, they're called).  I had 3 yesterday and the same today.  What I can give a plus to was I didn't feel so constantly hungry.  I did feel like doing more things during
the day..... both days.  I am going to continue until the 16 are GONE.  It does leave somewhat of a taste in your mouth - not so bad that it was a chore to drink the remainder - but it wasn't a milk shake.  I also should admit that I can be picky about my food so the fact I've had 6 of these so far is a good sign for me.  At the end of the 16, I shall decide if I am on my way to Amazon for more or off to try another action that might help this old body.  So, it's not over 'til.....

evidence_review:
I see that another reviewer has had the same reaction I had: it tastes like Metrecal.  Metrecal was a huge fad for weight loss among my parents' generation in the early 60s.  I have memories of adults trying it in the kitchen and all remarking that "it tastes just like a chocolate milkshake."  As a nine-year-old in 1961, I thought it tasted horrible.  Now comes this 100-calorie Boost unleashing a flood of memories, like Proust's madeleine, and yes it tastes like Metrecal, and yes, now that tastes like a chocolate milkshake.

I normally make a point of not reading any other reviews of the products I try because I don't want to prejudice my own review, but in this case I was (and still am) confused about how much this product costs.  I received 4 packages each with 4 of these little bottles - is this what they charge over $34 for 16 4 oz. bottles?  That seems rather expensive for what they are.

I'll probably keep these in the refrigerator at work for a late afternoon snack.  I had thought to give them to my 91-year-old mother but I think she would find them hard to open (the packaging is a little complex).  The 4 ounce dosage is not enough for me to use a meal replacement, but it's (probably) better for me than a candy bar.

evidence_review:
A few years ago my husband was in a nursing home - now called Skilled Nursing, which I suppose sounds better than NURSING home.
It was there while visiting him each day that I had my first taste of BOOST.  They gave it to him every time he wanted a drink and
often brought an extra for me.  I have to admit I don't prefer supplemental, energy or dietary drinks but at the time, they sufficed.

Now I am trying this out for an entirely different reason.  I now live in a retirement community and because some high-calorie things are
served in our dining room daily, I have gained weight.  So, someone told me that these  drinks could cut down on your calories, I
decided to give it a try.

Still not my favorite but neither are the extra pounds.  If I could add a scoop of vanilla ice cream this review would probably sound better.
But as that would defeat my purpose, I have been trying this Rich Chocolate Boost out.  Certainly it does not rank up there with the best
drink I ever had but considering all those vitamins, etc. I didn't expect much.  These are 4 oz cans (Compact, they're called).  I had 3 yesterday and the same today.  What I can give a plus to was I didn't feel so constantly hungry.  I did feel like doing more things during
the day..... both days.  I am going to continue until the 16 are GONE.  It does leave somewhat of a taste in your mouth - not so bad that it was a chore to drink the remainder - but it wasn't a milk shake.  I also should admit that I can be picky about my food so the fact I've had 6 of these so far is a good sign for me.  At the end of the 16, I shall decide if I am on my way to Amazon for more or off to try another action that might help this old body.  So, it's not over 'til.....

evidence_review:
I see that another reviewer has had the same reaction I had: it tastes like Metrecal.  Metrecal was a huge fad for weight loss among my parents' generation in the early 60s.  I have memories of adults trying it in the kitchen and all remarking that "it tastes just like a chocolate milkshake."  As a nine-year-old in 1961, I thought it tasted horrible.  Now comes this 100-calorie Boost unleashing a flood of memories, like Proust's madeleine, and yes it tastes like Metrecal, and yes, now that tastes like a chocolate milkshake.

I normally make a point of not reading any other reviews of the products I try because I don't want to prejudice my own review, but in this case I was (and still am) confused about how much this product costs.  I received 4 packages each with 4 of these little bottles - is this what they charge over $34 for 16 4 oz. bottles?  That seems rather expensive for what they are.

I'll probably keep these in the refrigerator at work for a late afternoon snack.  I had thought to give them to my 91-year-old mother but I think she would find them hard to open (the packaging is a little complex).  The 4 ounce dosage is not enough for me to use a meal replacement, but it's (probably) better for me than a candy bar.

Now I am trying this out for an entirely different reason.  I now live in a retirement community and because some high-calorie things are
served in our dining room daily, I have gained weight.  So, someone told me that these  drinks could cut down on your calories, I
decided to give it a try.

Still not my favorite but neither are the extra pounds.  If I could add a scoop of vanilla ice cream this review would probably sound better.

drink I ever had but considering all those vitamins, etc. I didn't expect much.  These are 4 oz cans (Compact, they're called).  I had 3 yesterday and the same today.  What I can give a plus to was I didn't feel so constantly hungry.  I did feel like doing more things during
the day..... both days.  I am going to continue until the 16 are GONE.  It does leave somewhat of a taste in your mouth - not so bad that it was a chore to drink the remainder - but it wasn't a milk shake.  I also should admit that I can be picky about my food so the fact I've had 6 of these so far is a good sign for me.  At the end of the 16, I shall decide if I am on my way to Amazon for more or off to try another action that might help this old body.  So, it's not over 'til.....

evidence_review:

I normally make a point of not reading any other reviews of the products I try because I don't want to prejudice my own review, but in this case I was (and still am) confused about how much this product costs.  I received 4 packages each with 4 of these little bottles - is this what they charge over $34 for 16 4 oz. bottles?  That seems rather expensive for what they are.

I'll probably keep these in the refrigerator at work for a late afternoon snack.  I had thought to give them to my 91-year-old mother but I think she would find them hard to open (the packaging is a little complex).  The 4 ounce dosage is not enough for me to use a meal replacement, but it's (probably) better for me than a candy bar.
